correctness.rationale: A weight-three cyclic binary word is a necklace of three ordered nonnegative zero gaps. For marker deletion, the two remaining gaps are unordered, yielding O as the number of distinct min(g,s-g). For zero deletion, distinct results are rotations of the three decremented triples. The only distinct positive-gap coincidences follow from one- and two-position cyclic shifts: all equal, or (t,t,t-1). These outputs have three ones and cannot collide with marker-deleted two-one outputs. A full case split and stars-and-bars/inclusion-exclusion and Burnside give each C_{s,j}, total, exact mean and asymptotics. A word-based checker independently corroborated every necklace at s<=36 (3055) and 450 larger cases. A finite test is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete and exact distribution of a natural observable in a well-motivated sparse cyclic one-deletion channel, for all lengths. Nontrivial rotation-orbit collisions distinguish degree four and five, a sharp degree-six threshold occurs at length nine, and the uniform-necklace mean tends to six with an explicit first correction. These give interpretable reconstruction/code-design sphere profiles rather than arbitrary small-number tables. No claim beyond the fixed-three-marker model is made.
